title: Today marks one year since the passing of Ken Balcomb, renowned resea...
description: Today marks one year since the passing of Ken Balcomb, renowned researcher & advocate for the Southern Resident killer whales. He devoted his life to helping this population & his work lives on through the Center for Whale Research and all of those who are advocating for the SRKW.  2023 brought two new calves to the population, L126 & L127. Every new birth brings hope. This population faces many threats, like lack of prey due to declining salmon populations & pollutants. The Robert Banks Terminal 2 expansion will increase the number of container ships in critical habitat & increase noise pollution impacts. Cruise ships dump waste & also increase noise pollution, which interferes with SRKW hunting/foraging, which can reduce their ability to hunt up to 5 hours per day. Pollution from contaminates & chemicals have made the SRKW one of the most contaminated mammal species in the world. These pollutants are associated with reproductive impairment & endocrine disruption. And their prey, salmon, face these same threats and many more due to climate change, habitat degradation, & unsustainable fisheries.  But there is still hope in the face of these threats. There are many people continually advocating & working to help salmon & SRKWs. Working together is how we will make the biggest impact. Taking action, big & small, has an impact.  We can prevent extinction for the SRKW.  Videos by @Orca Conservancy from our September encounter with J Pod off of San Juan Island. We sat on a dewy bench in the dark morning, listening to their blows, breaches, tail slaps, and the sounds of their calls on the hydrophone. It was the perfect morning & I treasure it forever. I wish I could fully share that experience but here is a little attempt 💕 #Orca #KillerWhale
